# Mahāsīhanāda Sutta (DN 8 (PTS DN i 161))

**ID:** DN 8 (PTS DN i 161)  
**Section:** Dīghanikāya (dn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Mahāsīhanāda Sutta  
**PTS:** DN i 161  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0101m.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0101m.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (DN 8), also widely known in the tradition as the *Kassapasīhanāda Sutta*, is the eighth discourse of the *Dīghanikāya* [Walshe 1987; Tournier et al. 2018]. In this sutta, the Buddha is questioned by a naked ascetic regarding the value of spiritual austerities (*tapa*); the Buddha clarifies that engaging in harsh self-mortification can easily occur without cultivating genuine purity of mind [Walshe 1987]. In modern philological scholarship, the sutta's opening PTS volume page (DN i 161) is referenced for the stock formula *sahadhammiko vādānuvādo garayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchati* [Nakamura 1980].

The text corresponds to a parallel in the Chinese *Dīrgha-āgama* (DĀ 25) and is represented by Sanskrit manuscript fragments (SHT sutta50, SF 51, SF 295). In addition, a palm-leaf manuscript fragment discovered in the Tibetan Autonomous Region preserves portions of an *Acelakamahāsūtra*, representing a Middle Indo-Aryan version corresponding directly to DN 8 [Tournier et al. 2018]. In the Pali canonical and paracanonical corpus, the sutta is cited or referenced in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 14, 15), *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 10.3, 18.9), and *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4).
